purpose: Loteprednol is a steroid eye drop used to treat eye inflammation, pain, and swelling. It is commonly used after eye surgery, or to treat eye allergies and other conditions that cause redness and irritation in the eyes. Your doctor may also prescribe it for certain eye infections when inflammation needs to be controlled.
how_it_works: This medication works by calming down the immune response in your eye that causes swelling, redness, and discomfort. Think of it like putting out a fire in your eye — it reduces the chemicals in your body that trigger inflammation. Because it works locally in the eye and is quickly broken down by the body, it tends to have fewer side effects than some other steroid eye drops.
common_side_effects: You may notice temporary blurry vision right after putting in the drops — this usually clears up quickly. Some people experience mild burning, stinging, or a feeling like something is in their eye. Redness, watery eyes, or a slight headache can also occur.
warnings: Do not wear soft contact lenses while using this medication unless your doctor says it is okay. Using steroid eye drops for too long can raise pressure inside your eye, which could harm your vision — your doctor will likely check your eye pressure if you use this for more than 10 days. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or have had eye infections in the past. Never share this medication with anyone else.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) about 4 times a day, but this can vary depending on why you are using it. After eye surgery, your doctor may start you at more frequent doses and then taper down. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's exact instructions, and try to use the drops at evenly spaced times throughout the day.
